mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 3.0% signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.0%, it indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.5%) combined with high consumer spending (RSAFS > 700000 million dollars) signals an overheating economy that triggers anticipated monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5% and RSAFS > 700000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when HOUST falls > 0.5% (m/m) during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A payroll employment growth rate (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% (m/m), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year) and elevated federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 3.5%) indicate aggressive monetary tightening that compresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% y/y and FEDFUNDS > 3.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Positive year-over-year growth in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 y/y growth is positive, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
